clue.text: Most of the elite in ancient Egypt

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but the end, so the final letter of the phrase for the elite goes

parts.note: the elite are the best people, the cream

explanation.surface: A remark that the ruling class of ancient Egypt was almost everyone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last T from THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, near modern Luxor, so it is a place found there.

parts.note: to hang someone is to execute them
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab is put to death inside a huge structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is a big shed for housing aircraft, a large building.

indicators.note: in places the street inside the word for blossom

parts.note: bloom means blossom
a road is a street

explanation.surface: Covering the road with a carpet of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven on a wide loom, so the word names a kind of carpet.

clue.text: Initially shrewd young rascal spilled the beans? Wally!

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of shrewd

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A sharp young scamp blabbed: what an idiot!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wally is a fool or idiot, which is what a simpleton is.

clue.text: Impose a curfew on office of proverbial confidant

parts.note: to gate a student is to confine them to college, a curfew-style punishment
a post is a job or office

explanation.surface: Confining someone indoors at the bureau of a trusted friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'between you and me and the gatepost' makes it the proverbial keeper of secrets. Gating is a British school and university punishment confining a student to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'between you and me and the gatepost' treats the post as the silent listener to a secret.

indicators.note: in puts the decay inside the word for an opening

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall
rot is decay or deterioration

explanation.surface: Something is decaying in the throttle valve of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throttle' looks like an engine part but is the verb meaning strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To garotte someone is to strangle them with a cord, so to throttle.

indicators.note: about means around, so the untruth goes round the grade letter

parts.note: a tale is a fib or lie
B is second class, after A

explanation.surface: Telling fibs about mediocre grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Table can mean the food served, as in a restaurant that keeps a good table.

definitions.meaning: to shanghai is to force into service

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out in a Chinese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing pesters a person; press-ganging, or shanghaiing, forced men into naval service.

parts.note: Serge is a name often used for a Russian man (Sergei)
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A Russian labourer is turned into a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned army rank, so a soldier of that rank.

parts.note: late as in 'the late chairman' means former

explanation.surface: Slipping in after the agreed time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale who reports on others, just like an informer.

indicators.note: restraining holds something in, so the king is held between the letters of 'by'

parts.note: taken as written
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Worn out by the effort of holding back a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exhausted has tired, bleary eyes, so the adjective stands for weary.

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A young museum-goer turns out to be a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A, the Victoria and Albert Museum, is a big London museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a destructive young offender, a kind of delinquent.

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman loathes seeing a sports cup smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ASHES is the urn for which England and Australia compete at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the famous prize in England–Australia Test cricket series, a sports trophy.

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A church garment is said to be heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white robe worn by clergy at services, a liturgical vestment.

clue.text: Working and, at that point, certain to be emotionally distressed

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
there means at that place or point
bound to be means certain to be

explanation.surface: Someone at work and at a particular moment is sure to be upset.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rebound describes someone still reeling from a broken relationship, so emotionally unsettled.

clue.text: Ostentatious cheer when wild boar is captured

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the shuffled animal sits in the word for cheer

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or delight

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of boar run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Hunters celebrate when a wild boar is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer' is a verb here, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means highly detailed and showy, so ornate or ostentatious.

indicators.note: modelled means shaped afresh, so the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A top fashion model posed for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European artist from before about 1800, so a painter.

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An appeal guaranteed to bring delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure and enjoyment are synonyms for the feeling of happy satisfaction.

clue.text: Traveller's joy seeing damn bad loser upset

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters of the three words over into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller enjoys watching a sore loser throw a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller's joy' looks like a feeling; it is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy and old man's beard are both common names of the wild clematis, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman, a sailor
the possessive ending supplies its own letter

explanation.surface: A seaman's well-toned physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Abs is informal for abdominal muscles, the stomach muscles.

parts.note: a band is a group or crew of people
saw means spotted, noticed

explanation.surface: The ship's crew sighted a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a boat; it is a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw is a power saw with a continuous blade loop, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Claim supporter tucked into the booze

indicators.note: tucked into puts the supporter inside the booze

parts.note: ale is beer, booze
a leg supports a table or body

explanation.surface: A football fan is getting stuck into the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan, but here it is a body part that holds you up.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or claim, typically without proof.

clue.text: A state of panic dogs Spike

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them
a pin is a small spike

explanation.surface: A dog called Spike is in a frantic mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is a spinning dive of an aircraft, and figuratively a loss of control or panic.

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the word for race

parts.note: to last is to run on or continue, as time races or runs
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The low spot of a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest in amount or degree, the lowest.

definitions.meaning: Laurence J. ... gave his name to the ... Principle, that people rise to their level of incompetence
old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A man of honour can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peter Principle is named after its author, and safecrackers were once called peter-men.

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a priestly source of prophecy, so a soothsayer or seer.

clue.text: Dog eats an oddity of nature

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the dog's letters surround the next word

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog swallows something strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutant is an organism changed by mutation, a freak or oddity of nature.

parts.note: to scan is to examine or check
ties are straps or fastenings

explanation.surface: Inspect the straps on a woman's lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanties is an informal term for skimpy knickers or lingerie worn by women.

clue.text: Delaware atomic project? That's the last place to live!

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware
A is the abbreviation for atomic, as in A-bomb
to project is to throw or hurl

explanation.surface: A nuclear programme in Delaware sounds like the worst neighbourhood imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun (a scheme) but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Death row is the prison block where condemned prisoners spend their final days, a grim last home.

clue.text: Hesitation about composer being a breadwinner

indicators.note: about here means around, so the hesitation goes round the composer

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
Thomas Arne wrote 'Rule, Britannia!'

explanation.surface: Pausing over whether a composer can support a family.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne is the English composer of 'Rule, Britannia!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadwinner is the person who brings in the household's income, its wage-earner.
